newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cossack oil platform eyes restart on Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cossack oil platform eyes restart on Jan 10.

text.p: The Cossack Pioneer floating oil platform hopes to return to its mooring in the Indian Ocean off Western Australia on Friday after disconnecting last Monday to flee the path of cyclone Rachel, a spokesman for operator Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Wednesday.
The cyclone has been downgraded by weather authorities to a rain-bearing depression after reaching land on Wednesday.

The Griffin floating oil platform, which headed west on Tuesday, remained disconnected at midday (0400 GMT) on Wednesday with no immediate plans to reconnect, a spokesman for the operator, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, said.
Oil production from Cossack Pioneer has been averaging about 90,000 barrels per day (bpd), while Griffin has been averaging around 70,000 bpd in recent weeks.
The spokesman for Cossack Pioneer said the platform had returned to the general vicinity of its mooring.
"The actual date for reconnecting would be determined sea conditions," he said.
The BHP spokesman said the company was monitoring sea conditions and would probably make a decision on Thursday on when to reconnect.
The cyclone, which at its strongest recorded wind gusts of about 180 km an hour, caused the loss of over 200,000 barrels of crude oil production a day.
It was the second cyclone to rip through the offshore oil and gas-producing regions of Western Australia in two weeks, disrupting production at oil platforms and on Barrow and Thevenard islands.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf, where the Cossack Pioneer is situated, are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside.
BHP holds a 45 percent interest in the Griffin oil project and is the operator. Mobil holds 35 percent and Inpex Alpha Ltd owns the remaining 20 percent.
